title: Chicken, drumstick, meat and skin, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks consist of meat and skin. In their raw state they are rich in protein, B‑vitamins, iron and zinc. Drumsticks are commonly used for roasting, frying, and braising.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Drumsticks contain more fat than chicken breast because of the skin.
The skin adds flavor and helps keep the meat juicy during cooking.
In many cuisines the drumsticks are marinated in spices and soy sauce before cooking.
Raw chicken can carry salmonella, making proper hygiene and cooking essential.
Drumsticks are often added to stocks for a richer broth.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth, repair, and a healthy immune system.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B3, B6 and B12 support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for blood formation and immune health.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Phosphorus in drumsticks works with calcium to strengthen bones.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: The fat in the skin supplies energy and aids absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Raw chicken may contain salmonella or campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C.

items.title: Higher fat content
items.content: Drumsticks are more calorie‑dense than lean cuts; watch portion sizes if weight management is a goal.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Drumsticks contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drumsticks can be baked, fried, braised, or grilled. The skin may be removed to reduce fat or left on for flavor. Marinating in lemon, garlic, herbs, and spices enhances taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw drumsticks in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in an airtight container for up to 2 days. For longer storage freeze at ‑18 °C; they remain good for up to 9 months. Thaw frozen drumsticks in the fridge before cooking.
